title: [Event Request] Missing OnApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLinesOnAfterValidateType event
description:
### Why do you need this change?

Table 172 "Standard Customer Sales Code" exposes `OnApplyStdCodesToSalesLinesOnAfterValidateType` inside `ApplyStdCodesToSalesLines`. This event fires immediately after `Type` is validated on the newly inserted sales line, allowing extensions to react to or complement the type validation — for example, to set custom default values, apply additional field logic, or integrate with third-party modules that depend on the line type being resolved before further fields are set.

Table 175 "Standard Vendor Purchase Code" has a symmetric procedure `ApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLines` but is missing the equivalent event. Extensions that extend both the sales and purchase recurring-code flow are unable to implement consistent behavior on the purchase side.

There is no existing event in `ApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLines` that fires at the same point in the flow (after type validation, before additional field assignments such as `No.` validation):

| Existing event | Position | Sufficient? |
|---|---|---|
| `OnBeforeApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLines` | Before loop | Too early |
| `OnApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLinesOnBeforeStdPurchLineFind` | Before per-line processing | Too early |
| `OnApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLinesOnAfterPurchLineInsert` | After insert, all fields set | Too late |
| `OnAfterApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLines` | After full loop | Too late |

### Describe the request

### EventRequest


[W1][Table][175][Standard Vendor Purchase Code]
[ApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLines]
___

Add a missing integration event equivalent to
OnApplyStdCodesToSalesLinesOnAfterValidateType in Table 172.
The event should fire immediately after PurchLine.Validate(Type)
inside the ApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLines loop, passing the current
purchase line and the standard purchase line as parameters.
___
```al

[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLinesOnAfterValidateType(
    var PurchaseLine: Record "Purchase Line";
    StandardPurchaseLine: Record "Standard Purchase Line")
begin
end;
```

### Proposed placement (pseudocode context)

```al
// inside ApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLines loop:
PurchLine.Validate(Type, StdPurchLine.Type);
OnApplyStdCodesToPurchaseLinesOnAfterValidateType(PurchLine, StdPurchLine);  // <-- new
PurchLine.Validate("No.", StdPurchLine."No.");
```

### Symmetry reference — Table 172 existing event

```al
// Table 172 "Standard Customer Sales Code";
[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnApplyStdCodesToSalesLinesOnAfterValidateType(
    var SalesLine: Record "Sales Line";
    StandardSalesLine: Record "Standard Sales Line")
begin
end;
```

The requested event is a direct purchase-side mirror of this existing sales-side event.

title: [W1][Codeunit][5988][Serv-Documents Mgt.] OnAfter events when the posted Service Invoice Line / Service Cr.Memo Line is inserted in FinalizeInvoiceDocument / FinalizeCrMemoDocument
description:
## Why do you need this change?

Our app keeps a companion table linked to posted document lines by SystemId. During posting we have to capture which posted line belongs to which source document line.

In Sales and Purchase the posted line is inserted directly into the real table, and events such as `OnAfterSalesInvLineInsert` / `OnAfterSalesCrMemoLineInsert` (codeunit 80) give the persisted posted line with its final SystemId.

Service posting works differently. Codeunit 5988 "Serv-Documents Mgt." first inserts the posted lines into **temporary** records (`PrepareInvoiceLine`, `PrepareCrMemoLine`), so the line in `OnAfterServInvLineInsert` / `OnAfterServCrMemoLineInsert` is temporary. Later, `FinalizeInvoiceDocument` / `FinalizeCrMemoDocument` copy the temporary lines into the real tables, and only then is the final SystemId assigned. For shipments there is already an event at exactly that point, `OnFinalizeShipmentDocumentOnAfterInserServiceShipmentLine(var ServiceShipmentLine2)`, but the invoice and credit memo loops have none.

Our workaround: we buffer the line numbers in a SingleInstance codeunit during `OnAfterServInvLineInsert` / `OnAfterServCrMemoLineInsert`, then re-read the posted lines in `OnAfterFinalizeInvoiceDocument` / `OnAfterFinalizeCrMemoDocument`. This works, but it needs a second pass over the lines and state that lives across events. Adding the missing events makes the three Finalize loops consistent.

## Describe the request

Add a per-line `OnAfter` event in the invoice and credit memo copy loops, mirroring the existing shipment event. The two changes are in the same codeunit and serve the same scenario.

```AL
[W1][Codeunit][5988][Serv-Documents Mgt.]
procedure FinalizeInvoiceDocument
___

Raise an event after each ServiceInvoiceLine2.Insert(), like OnFinalizeShipmentDocumentOnAfterInserServiceShipmentLine in FinalizeShipmentDocument.
___

            ServInvLine.Reset();
            if ServInvLine.Find('-') then
                repeat
                    ServiceInvoiceLine2.Init();
                    ServiceInvoiceLine2.Copy(ServInvLine);
                    ServiceInvoiceLine2.Insert();
                    OnFinalizeInvoiceDocumentOnAfterInsertServiceInvoiceLine(ServiceInvoiceLine2); // new
                until ServInvLine.Next() = 0;
            ServInvLine.DeleteAll();

[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnFinalizeInvoiceDocumentOnAfterInsertServiceInvoiceLine(var ServiceInvoiceLine: Record "Service Invoice Line")
begin
end;
```

```AL
[W1][Codeunit][5988][Serv-Documents Mgt.]
procedure FinalizeCrMemoDocument
___

Raise an event after each PServCrMemoLine.Insert().
___

            ServCrMemoLine.Reset();
            if ServCrMemoLine.Find('-') then
                repeat
                    PServCrMemoLine.Init();
                    PServCrMemoLine.Copy(ServCrMemoLine);
                    PServCrMemoLine.Insert();
                    OnFinalizeCrMemoDocumentOnAfterInsertServiceCrMemoLine(PServCrMemoLine); // new
                until ServCrMemoLine.Next() = 0;
            ServCrMemoLine.DeleteAll();

[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnFinalizeCrMemoDocumentOnAfterInsertServiceCrMemoLine(var ServiceCrMemoLine: Record "Service Cr.Memo Line")
begin
end;
```

Notes:
- No IsHandled, no behavior change. Raised once per posted line, inside a loop that already inserts each line, with no extra reads.
- The posted line data is already exposed by the existing `OnAfterServInvLineInsert` / `OnAfterServCrMemoLineInsert` events, so nothing new or sensitive is exposed.

title: [W1][MultiObjects] Service Line - InitType() with OnAfterInitType, used by the service line pages that carry over the line Type
description:
## Why do you need this change?

When a user creates a new line on a document, Business Central carries over the `Type` of the previous line. Our app adds G/L Account lines that belong to an item or resource line. After such a G/L line, the next new line should get the type of the item or resource line it belongs to, not "G/L Account". Otherwise users have to change the Type on every next line.

Sales and Purchase support this. Table 37 "Sales Line" and table 39 "Purchase Line" have a public `InitType()` that the subforms call from `OnNewRecord`, and it raises `OnAfterInitType(var SalesLine; xSalesLine; SalesHeader)` (plus `OnBeforeInitType`).

Table 5902 "Service Line" has no `InitType()`. The pages set the type inline in `OnNewRecord`:

```AL
    trigger OnNewRecord(BelowxRec: Boolean)
    begin
        Rec.Type := xRec.Type;
        Clear(ShortcutDimCode);
    end;
```

As a result there is no single extensibility point for the default Type of a new service line. The only option is to subscribe to the `OnNewRecordEvent` trigger event of every page that carries over the Type (5907, 5934, 5936). That spreads the same logic over several page subscribers, misses any page added later, and differs from how Sales and Purchase are extended. A table-level `InitType()` gives one hook in one place, the same way it works for Sales and Purchase.

## Describe the request

Move the existing inline logic into a new `InitType()` procedure on table 5902 "Service Line" that raises `OnAfterInitType`, and call it from the pages that carry over the Type today. The table procedure and the page calls depend on each other, so they are one request. There is no behavior change: `InitType()` does exactly what the pages do today.

We deliberately request only an `OnAfter` event, not an IsHandled event. Subscribers can set `Type` after the default is applied.

```AL
[W1][Table][5902][Service Line]
new procedure InitType
___

New public procedure with the logic that is currently inline in the pages' OnNewRecord, and an OnAfter event.
___

    procedure InitType()
    begin
        Type := xRec.Type;

        OnAfterInitType(Rec, xRec);
    end;

[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnAfterInitType(var ServiceLine: Record "Service Line"; xServiceLine: Record "Service Line")
begin
end;
```

```AL
[W1][Page][5934][Service Invoice Subform]
trigger OnNewRecord
___

Call Rec.InitType() instead of the inline assignment.
Identical change in page 5936 "Service Credit Memo Subform" and page 5907 "Service Item Worksheet Subform".
___

    trigger OnNewRecord(BelowxRec: Boolean)
    begin
        Rec.InitType(); // was: Rec.Type := xRec.Type;
        Clear(ShortcutDimCode);
    end;
```

Notes:
- Pages 5905 "Service Lines" and 5966 "Service Quote Lines" do not carry over the Type today. We do not ask to change that.
- Runs once per new line in the UI. No extra reads, no sensitive data.

Related requests (Service parity with Sales/Purchase, same scenario family): #13250 (Undo corrective line events), #13250 (service line pages OnAfterNoOnAfterValidate), #13250 (Serv-Documents Mgt. finalize line events)

title: [W1][MultiObjects] Undo Service Shipment Line / Undo Service Consumption Line - OnAfter event after the corrective Service Shipment Line is inserted
description:
## Why do you need this change?

Our app stores data in a companion table that is linked to document lines and posted document lines by SystemId. When a posted line is undone, we must copy that data from the original posted line to the new corrective line, so we need both records at the moment the corrective line is inserted.

For Sales and Purchase this is possible with the existing events raised right after the corrective line insert:
- Codeunit 5815 "Undo Sales Shipment Line": `OnAfterNewSalesShptLineInsert(var NewSalesShipmentLine; OldSalesShipmentLine)`
- Codeunit 5813 "Undo Purchase Receipt Line": `OnAfterNewPurchRcptLineInsert(...)`
- "Undo Return Shipment Line" / "Undo Return Receipt Line": `OnAfterNewReturnShptLineInsert(...)` / `OnAfterNewReturnRcptLineInsert(...)`

The Service equivalents have no such event:
- Codeunit 5818 "Undo Service Shipment Line" raises `OnBeforeNewServiceShptLineInsert(NewServShptLine, OldServShptLine)` before the insert, but nothing after it. The later `OnAfterInsertNewShipmentLine` in `Code` only receives the **old** line, so the new line (and its SystemId) is not available.
- Codeunit 5819 "Undo Service Consumption Line" raises `OnInsertCorrectiveShipmentLineOnBeforeInsert(...)` before the insert, but nothing after it.

Before the insert the SystemId is not assigned yet. As a workaround we now search for the corrective line afterwards with a filter (`Correction = true`, same `Document No.` and `Order Line No.`, greater `Line No.`). This is fragile when several lines are undone in one run and it costs an extra read per line. Any extension that keeps line-level data keyed by SystemId (or that needs to copy custom data to the corrective line after insert) has the same gap in Service.

## Describe the request

Add one `OnAfter` integration event directly after the corrective Service Shipment Line is inserted, in both codeunits, mirroring `OnAfterNewSalesShptLineInsert`. Both objects are in one request because it is the same change for the same scenario (undoing posted service lines).

```AL
[W1][Codeunit][5818][Undo Service Shipment Line]
procedure InsertNewShipmentLine
___

Raise an event after NewServShptLine.Insert(), with the new and the old line (same signature as OnBeforeNewServiceShptLineInsert).
___

        NewServShptLine.Correction := true;
        NewServShptLine."Dimension Set ID" := OldServShptLine."Dimension Set ID";
        OnBeforeNewServiceShptLineInsert(NewServShptLine, OldServShptLine);
        NewServShptLine.Insert();
        OnAfterNewServiceShptLineInsert(NewServShptLine, OldServShptLine); // new

        InsertItemEntryRelation(TempGlobalItemEntryRelation, NewServShptLine);
    end;

[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnAfterNewServiceShptLineInsert(var NewServiceShipmentLine: Record "Service Shipment Line"; OldServiceShipmentLine: Record "Service Shipment Line")
begin
end;
```

```AL
[W1][Codeunit][5819][Undo Service Consumption Line]
procedure InsertCorrectiveShipmentLine
___

Raise an event after NewServiceShipmentLine.Insert(), with the new and the old line (same signature as OnInsertCorrectiveShipmentLineOnBeforeInsert).
___

        NewServiceShipmentLine.Correction := true;

        OnInsertCorrectiveShipmentLineOnBeforeInsert(NewServiceShipmentLine, OldServiceShipmentLine);
        NewServiceShipmentLine.Insert();
        OnInsertCorrectiveShipmentLineOnAfterInsert(NewServiceShipmentLine, OldServiceShipmentLine); // new

        UpdateItemJnlLine(NewServiceShipmentLine, ItemShptEntryNo);
        if OldServiceShipmentLine.Type = OldServiceShipmentLine.Type::Item then begin

[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnInsertCorrectiveShipmentLineOnAfterInsert(var NewServiceShipmentLine: Record "Service Shipment Line"; OldServiceShipmentLine: Record "Service Shipment Line")
begin
end;
```

Notes:
- No IsHandled, no behavior change. Raised once per undone line, with no extra database reads.
- The records are already in scope at that point, and no sensitive data is exposed.

Related requests (Service parity with Sales/Purchase, same scenario family): #13251 (service line pages OnAfterNoOnAfterValidate), #13252 (Service Line InitType), #13253 (Serv-Documents Mgt. finalize line events)

title: [EventRequest][W1][table][7003][Price Asset] New event OnBeforeValidateVariantCode in OnValidate trigger of field "Variant Code"
description:
### Why do you need this change?

Problem statement:

A customization must control the validation of the "Variant Code" field in table 7003 "Price Asset".

The existing table-level OnValidate trigger requires "Asset Type" to be Item when "Variant Code" is populated. However, the customization must also support validating a variant code when:

AL
`"Asset Type" <> "Asset Type"::Item`

There is currently no extensibility point that allows an extension to handle the validation and prevent the standard `TestField()` and `ValidateAssetNo()` calls from being executed.

Alternatives evaluated:
Tried the existing `OnBeforeValidate` event in table 7003 "Price Asset", but it was not sufficient because raising an error terminates the complete process instead of allowing the extension to provide replacement validation.
Considered modifying the `"Variant Code"` field through a table extension, but an additional validation trigger cannot prevent the original table field's `OnValidate trigger` from running.
Considered using a page-level validation trigger, but table validation can also be invoked from AL code and processes that do not use a page.
Considered a standard integration event without `IsHandled`, but it could not prevent the existing `TestField()` and `ValidateAssetNo()` calls.
Considered adding a new field or action, but this would duplicate the existing `"Variant Code"` functionality and would not address validation initiated outside the UI.

### Describe the request

Proposed publisher location:

```
 Object: Table 7003 "Price Asset"
 Namespace: Microsoft.Pricing.Asset
 Field: 6 "Variant Code", Code[10]
 Procedure: Field-level OnValidate trigger
```

Placement rationale:

The event should be placed at the beginning of the `"Variant Code"` field's table-level OnValidate trigger.

This placement allows a subscriber to provide replacement validation before the following standard logic is executed:

AL
```
TestField("Asset Type", "Asset Type"::Item);
TestField("Asset No.");
ValidateAssetNo();
```

When the subscriber sets `IsHandled := true`, the trigger exits before the standard validation and its related side effects occur.

Proposed code snippet (before -> after):
Before
AL
```
field(6; "Variant Code"; Code[10])
{
   Caption = 'Variant Code';
   DataClassification = SystemMetadata;
 
   trigger OnValidate()
   begin
      if "Variant Code" <> '' then begin
         TestField("Asset Type", "Asset Type"::Item);
         TestField("Asset No.");
        end;
 
      ValidateAssetNo();
   end;
}
```
After
AL
```
field(6; "Variant Code"; Code[10])
{
   Caption = 'Variant Code';
   DataClassification = SystemMetadata;
 
   trigger OnValidate()
   var
      IsHandled: Boolean;
   begin
      IsHandled := false;
      OnBeforeValidateVariantCode(Rec, IsHandled);
      if IsHandled then
         exit;
 
      if "Variant Code" <> '' then begin
         TestField("Asset Type", "Asset Type"::Item);
         TestField("Asset No.");
      end;
 
      ValidateAssetNo();
   end;
}
```
Proposed event publisher
AL
```
[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnBeforeValidateVariantCode(var PriceAsset: Record "Price Asset"; var IsHandled: Boolean)
begin
end;
```
Subscriber example (illustrative):
AL
```
[EventSubscriber(ObjectType::Table, Database::"Price Asset", OnBeforeValidateVariantCode, '', false, false)]
local procedure PriceAssetOnBeforeValidateVariantCode(var PriceAsset: Record "Price Asset"; var IsHandled: Boolean)
begin
   if IsHandled then
   exit;
 
   if PriceAsset."Asset Type" = PriceAsset."Asset Type"::Item then
   exit;
 
   // Custom validation or replacement logic
 
   IsHandled := true;
end;
```
Performance & data considerations:

The event is raised whenever field 6 "Variant Code" is validated on a temporary Price Asset record.

Table 7003 "Price Asset" has `TableType = Temporary`, and the expected number of records per process is two:

```
PriceAsset
PriceAssetInterface
```

The publisher does not introduce database operations, loops, locking, or external calls. It only invokes the integration event and evaluates the IsHandled variable. The expected performance impact is minimal.

The intended subscriber performs validation comparable to the existing OnValidate logic.

The event exposes the current temporary Price Asset record. The table has `DataClassification = CustomerContent`, while `"Variant Code"` has `DataClassification = SystemMetadata`. No previous record state or additional data is exposed.

Multi-extension interaction:

Multiple extensions could subscribe to `OnBeforeValidateVariantCode`.

Each subscriber should first check whether the validation has already been handled:

AL
```
if IsHandled then
   exit;
```

A subscriber should only set `IsHandled := true` after completing its replacement validation. Subscribers must not reset IsHandled from true to false.

If multiple extensions intend to replace the validation, the first subscriber that sets `IsHandled := true` prevents the standard validation from running. Subscriber execution order is not guaranteed.

Conflicts are mitigated by:

Checking `IsHandled` before executing subscriber logic.
Handling only the specific condition where `"Asset Type"` is not Item.
Leaving IsHandled unchanged for all unrelated records.
Not relying on a particular subscriber execution order.
Justification for using IsHandled over alternatives:

A standard integration event could add logic before or after the existing validation, but it could not prevent the following code from running:

AL
```
if "Variant Code" <> '' then begin
   TestField("Asset Type", "Asset Type"::Item);
   TestField("Asset No.");
end;
 
ValidateAssetNo();
```

The customization must support variant-code validation when `"Asset Type"` is not Item. This is currently prevented by the existing TestField("Asset Type", "Asset Type"::Item) call.

A table extension cannot replace the original field's `OnValidate trigger`. Redesigning the flow through an interface, strategy pattern, or separate validation procedure would require wider changes to the `"Price List Line"` processing, while the `"Unit of Measure Code"` field already uses comparable validation logic.

The subscriber only requires the current Price Asset record. xRec is not required and is intentionally excluded from the event signature.

Placing an IsHandled event at the beginning of the "Variant Code" field's OnValidate trigger is therefore the smallest self-contained change that allows the extension to replace the standard validation without modifying unrelated processing.

title: [IT][Extensibility Request] Expose a cloud-safe API to generate the standard FatturaPA payload
description:
### Why do you need this change?

We are implementing a **pre-posting FatturaPA preview and validation** capability for Sales Invoices / Credit Memos in Business Central SaaS.

The requirement is to let an extension generate the same standard outbound FatturaPA XML payload that Business Central would produce, so that it can be inspected, validated, and rendered before the document is posted or transmitted.

The current Italian localization already contains the standard FatturaPA serializer in codeunit `12179 "Export FatturaPA Document"`.

The relevant procedure is:

```al
[Scope('OnPrem')]
procedure GenerateXMLFile(
    var TempBlob: Codeunit "Temp Blob";
    var TempFatturaLine: Record "Fattura Line" temporary;
    TempFatturaHeader: Record "Fattura Header" temporary;
    ClientFileName: Text[250])
```

This procedure already accepts prepared temporary `Fattura Header` and `Fattura Line` buffers and serializes them using Microsoft's standard implementation, but it cannot be called from a SaaS extension because it is scoped `OnPrem`.

Duplicating the FatturaPA serializer in an extension would be undesirable because it would duplicate Microsoft-owned logic for:

- XML structure and element ordering;
- formatting;
- schema-related behavior;
- standard integration events;
- future FatturaPA changes.

A supported public SaaS boundary would allow extensions to reuse the authoritative Business Central serializer instead.

### Describe the request

Please expose a **cloud-safe public API for generating the standard outbound Italian FatturaPA payload from extension-prepared document data**.

For the current implementation, the narrowest solution could be to expose an equivalent of:

```al
procedure GenerateXMLFile(
    var TempBlob: Codeunit "Temp Blob";
    var TempFatturaLine: Record "Fattura Line" temporary;
    TempFatturaHeader: Record "Fattura Header" temporary;
    ClientFileName: Text[250])
```

without `Scope('OnPrem')`, provided that this remains the appropriate supported API.

The exact implementation is not essential to the request.

Business Central 2027 release wave 1 includes the planned Italian move to the newer **E-Documents / SDI framework**. If the FatturaPA serialization architecture is changing as part of that work, we would prefer the equivalent supported API in the new architecture rather than exposing a legacy method that is going to be superseded.

The required contract is:

> Given extension-prepared data representing an Italian electronic invoice, generate the same standard outbound FatturaPA payload that Business Central would generate for transmission, without actually transmitting or posting the document.

The API should be usable from a Business Central Cloud extension.

For preview scenarios it should also avoid side effects associated with actual transmission, in particular consuming or permanently assigning transmission/progressive numbering merely to inspect the generated document.

This would allow extensions to:

- preview the exact outbound FatturaPA XML;
- validate it before posting/transmission;
- render it using the official Agenzia delle Entrate transformation;
- reuse Microsoft's standard serializer rather than maintain a parallel one;
- automatically inherit future changes to the Italian electronic-invoicing implementation.

The current code is located in the Italian Base Application layer, currently under:

```text
src/Layers/IT/BaseApp/Local/EServices/EDocument/ExportFatturaPADocument.Codeunit.al
```

This request was originally submitted as:

`microsoft/ALAppExtensions#30404`

and has been recreated in BCApps at Microsoft's request after the ALAppExtensions issue was closed with:

> Please recreate your request in BCApps.


#### Clarification: preparation and serialization scope

The desired supported scenario includes **both preparation and serialization**.

Making `GenerateXMLFile(...)` SaaS-callable for already-prepared temporary `Fattura Header` and `Fattura Line` records would solve the serialization boundary, but by itself it would still require an extension to reproduce Microsoft's standard document-to-Fattura-buffer preparation logic.

For the pre-posting preview/validation scenario, we would therefore also need a **SaaS-safe, side-effect-free way to prepare the standard temporary Fattura data from the source document**, or an equivalent higher-level API that performs preparation and serialization together.

The important requirement is that preview generation must not consume or permanently assign values whose purpose is actual transmission, such as the next FatturaPA progressive number.

Conceptually, the supported flow should allow an extension to:

1. prepare the standard FatturaPA data for a source document using Microsoft's standard logic, without transmission-related side effects;
2. generate the standard outbound XML from that prepared data;
3. inspect, validate, or render the result without posting or transmitting the document.

If Microsoft prefers a single higher-level API that performs those operations internally rather than exposing separate preparation and serialization APIs, that would also satisfy the requirement.

Likewise, if the forthcoming E-Documents / SDI implementation provides an equivalent side-effect-free “prepare outbound document/payload” boundary, that would be preferable to exposing legacy APIs solely for this purpose.

The core requirement is therefore not specifically to expose `GenerateXMLFile(...)` alone, but to provide a supported SaaS path to obtain the authoritative standard outbound FatturaPA payload **without triggering posting, transmission, or irreversible numbering side effects**.

comment 2: [[Author] (2026-10-22)]: Thanks for the review. Answers to both points:

### 1. Why `RecordRef` instead of typed record parameters

**Consistency with this codeunit.** The events that already exist in the same area pass the header as `RecordRef`: `OnAfterInsertApplicableHeaderTradeAgreement(var HeaderTradeAgreementElement: XmlElement; HeaderRecordRef: RecordRef)` and `OnInsertPaymentMethodOnBeforeAddToRoot(var PaymentMethodElement: XmlElement; HeaderRecRef: RecordRef)`. `InsertApplicableHeaderTradeAgreement`, where event 1 is raised, already receives the header as `Variant` and works on a `RecordRef` internally.

**Four source document types.** The export handles Sales Invoice, Sales Cr.Memo, Service Invoice and Service Cr.Memo. Typed parameters would need one event per document type and hook, so 3 hooks × 4 types = 12 events. With only 3 × 2 = 6 events, service documents would keep arriving with the converted sales header, which is the problem raised in point 2. With `RecordRef` there are 3 events, and a further document type needs no new events.

**How subscribers use it.** Check `HeaderRecordRef.Number()` and convert with `SetTable`, or read fields that have the same number in all headers through `Field()`, as `GetBuyerReference` already does for "Buyer Reference" and "Your Reference":

```al
[EventSubscriber(ObjectType::Codeunit, Codeunit::"Export ZUGFeRD Document", 'OnInsertApplicableHeaderTradeDeliveryOnBeforeCreateElement', '', false, false)]
local procedure SetActualDeliveryDate(HeaderRecordRef: RecordRef; var ShipToName: Text[100]; var ShipToAddress: Record "Standard Address"; var DeliveryGLN: Code[13]; var ActualDeliveryDate: Date)
var
    SalesInvoiceHeader: Record "Sales Invoice Header";
    ServiceInvoiceHeader: Record "Service Invoice Header";
begin
    case HeaderRecordRef.Number() of
        Database::"Sales Invoice Header":
            begin
                HeaderRecordRef.SetTable(SalesInvoiceHeader);
                ActualDeliveryDate := GetPostedShipmentDate(SalesInvoiceHeader);
            end;
        Database::"Service Invoice Header":
            begin
                HeaderRecordRef.SetTable(ServiceInvoiceHeader);
                ActualDeliveryDate := GetPostedShipmentDate(ServiceInvoiceHeader);
            end;
    end;
end;
```

**Alternatives considered.**

- *Typed events per document type*: Not chosen, because this codeunit already uses `RecordRef` in these procedures and typed events would multiply the number of events (see above). The companion request for XRechnung (#13175) does use typed events, because most events of codeunit 13916 are typed.
- *`Variant` parameter*: no benefit over `RecordRef`, the subscriber still has to convert it, and the existing events use `RecordRef`.
- *Editing the finished document* in `OnCreateXMLOnBeforeSalesInvXmlDocumentWriteToFile`: this is today's workaround, which this request wants to replace (see "Why do you need this change?").

### 2. Service documents

Yes, all three events receive `SourceDocumentRecordRef` when it is set, and the passed sales header only as fallback for direct calls of `InsertSupplyChainTradeTransaction` without `CreateXML`. This is the pattern `InsertPaymentMethod` already uses for `OnInsertPaymentMethodOnBeforeAddToRoot` ([ExportZUGFeRDDocument.Codeunit.al#L1282-L1288](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/12c23610f39f91c03be67e21a15354d15ebc05ab/src/Apps/DE/EDocumentDE/app/src/ZUGFeRD/ExportZUGFeRDDocument.Codeunit.al#L1282-L1288)).

The converted sales header is not sufficient: `TransferRecordFields` copies fields by field number only, so fields of the service header without a field of the same number, type and length in the sales header do not reach the subscriber. The subscriber also cannot tell from the converted header that the document is a service document.

Details:

- The fallback logic is implemented once in a local helper and used by all three events.
- The `var` values (buyer, delivery) are still collected from the converted sales header, as today. Only the record passed as context is the original document.
- The existing `OnAfterInsertApplicableHeaderTradeAgreement` stays unchanged. It passes the converted header for service documents; changing that would alter the behavior for existing subscribers.

### Also updated

The description no longer depends on #12268: event 2 is now specified against the current main branch, and the scope is stated explicitly in the notes. I have updated the issue description accordingly.

title: [W1][Event Request] Codeunit 8062 "Billing Proposal" and table 8052 "Customer Subscription Contract" - control the billing period of a single subscription line
description:
### Why do you need this change?

Our extension pauses billing for one subscription line from a given date and aligns one line's billing to another line's term end (co-terming). For both we have to change one line's billing period inside a normal billing proposal run, without a separate run per line.

The current extension points do not allow this:

1. `OnCheckSkipSubscriptionLineOnElse` is raised only in the `else` branch of the `case true of` in `ProcessServiceCommitment`. It is not raised for usage-based lines or when an earlier branch matched, and it gets no billing dates.
2. No event is raised after `CalculateBillingPeriod` for normal lines (#11327 added one for usage-based lines only). `OnAfterCalculateNextBillingToDateForSubscriptionLine` changes the end of every rhythm step. A partner cannot cap the whole period once, and the `BillToDate <> 0D` path exits before any event.
3. In `UpdateBillingLine` the next period starts at `CalculateNextToDate("Billing Rhythm", "Billing from") + 1`, not at `"Billing to" + 1`. When a step was shortened, the days between the shortened `"Billing to"` and the rhythm end are never billed, and no event allows correcting the start date.
4. In harmonized billing, `FindEarliestServiceCommitment` takes the open line with the earliest Next Billing Date as the anchor. That includes lines already billed up to their end date (paused or terminated lines). Such a line becomes the anchor, and the anchor is wrong. We correct the anchor afterward in `OnAfterUpdateHarmonizedBillingFields`, which runs after the contract fields have already been calculated.

### Describe the request

All four are plain integration events. There is no IsHandled.

**1. Codeunit 8062 "Billing Proposal", `ProcessServiceCommitment`**: [L341-394](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/27f13242ac335d7d2204ead00a715ee18e4cc828/src/Apps/W1/Subscription%20Billing/App/Billing/Codeunits/BillingProposal.Codeunit.al#L341-L394). Raise after the `case true of ... end;` (after L388) and before `if not SkipServiceCommitment then`, so it runs for every branch:

```al
[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnProcessSubscriptionLineOnAfterCheckSkipSubscriptionLine(var SubscriptionLine: Record "Subscription Line"; BillingTemplate: Record "Billing Template"; BillingDate: Date; BillingToDate: Date; var SkipSubscriptionLine: Boolean)
begin
end;
```

Call: `OnProcessSubscriptionLineOnAfterCheckSkipSubscriptionLine(ServiceCommitment, BillingTemplate, BillingDate, BillingToDate, SkipServiceCommitment);`

**2. Same procedure, directly after `CalculateBillingPeriod(...)`** ([L390](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/27f13242ac335d7d2204ead00a715ee18e4cc828/src/Apps/W1/Subscription%20Billing/App/Billing/Codeunits/BillingProposal.Codeunit.al#L390)) and before `BillingLine.InitNewBillingLine()`. This covers all three exit paths of [`CalculateBillingPeriod` (L583-618)](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/27f13242ac335d7d2204ead00a715ee18e4cc828/src/Apps/W1/Subscription%20Billing/App/Billing/Codeunits/BillingProposal.Codeunit.al#L583-L618) without restructuring it:

```al
[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnProcessSubscriptionLineOnAfterCalculateBillingPeriod(SubscriptionLine: Record "Subscription Line"; BillingTemplate: Record "Billing Template"; BillingDate: Date; BillingToDate: Date; var BillingPeriodStart: Date; var BillingPeriodEnd: Date)
begin
end;
```

Call: `OnProcessSubscriptionLineOnAfterCalculateBillingPeriod(ServiceCommitment, BillingTemplate, BillingDate, BillingToDate, BillingPeriodStart, BillingPeriodEnd);`

**3. Same codeunit, `UpdateBillingLine`**: [L415-465](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/27f13242ac335d7d2204ead00a715ee18e4cc828/src/Apps/W1/Subscription%20Billing/App/Billing/Codeunits/BillingProposal.Codeunit.al#L415-L465). Raise after `NewBillingFromDate2` is final (after L452) and before `NewBillingToDate2 := CalculateNextBillingToDateForServiceCommitment(...)` (L454):

```al
[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnUpdateBillingLineOnAfterCalculateNextBillingFromDate(SubscriptionLine: Record "Subscription Line"; BillingLine: Record "Billing Line"; BillingTemplate: Record "Billing Template"; BillingPeriodEnd: Date; var NextBillingFromDate: Date)
begin
end;
```

Call: `OnUpdateBillingLineOnAfterCalculateNextBillingFromDate(ServiceCommitment, BillingLine, BillingTemplate, BillingPeriodEnd, NewBillingFromDate2);`. A subscriber that sets `NextBillingFromDate` after `BillingPeriodEnd` ends the recursion through the existing check at L422.

**4. Table 8052 "Customer Subscription Contract", `FindEarliestServiceCommitment`**: [L2268-2276](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/27f13242ac335d7d2204ead00a715ee18e4cc828/src/Apps/W1/Subscription%20Billing/App/Customer%20Contracts/Tables/CustomerSubscriptionContract.Table.al#L2268-L2276). Raise before `ServiceCommitmentFound := ServiceCommitment.FindFirst();`:

```al
[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnFindEarliestServiceCommitmentOnBeforeFindFirst(var SubscriptionLine: Record "Subscription Line"; CustomerSubscriptionContract: Record "Customer Subscription Contract"; DeletedCustContractLineNo: Integer)
begin
end;
```

Call: `OnFindEarliestServiceCommitmentOnBeforeFindFirst(ServiceCommitment, Rec, DeletedCustContractLineNo);`

Independent of the event, you may want to skip lines whose Next Billing Date is after their Subscription Line End Date (fully billed) in this search. Such a line cannot be the next billing anchor.

### Execution context

Checked on `main` [4c2cd71](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/4c2cd7171f1e1c41bcb5f5893f67589d71719050/src/Apps/W1/Subscription%20Billing/App/Billing/Codeunits/BillingProposal.Codeunit.al) (the line numbers above are unchanged there) and on `releases/29.0`.

**Yes, the three codeunit 8062 events should fire in every context that reaches them.** Our subscribers apply rules that belong to the subscription line, not to the run: a hold from a date, a co-term date, a line that waits for activation. If the events fired only in a template run, the same held line would still be billed from a contract or onto a purchase invoice. A "Billing to" change would also bring back the gap that event 3 closes.

| Caller in codeunit 8062 | Started from | Events reached | `BillingTemplate` | `SubscriptionLine` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateBillingProposal` ([L237](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/4c2cd7171f1e1c41bcb5f5893f67589d71719050/src/Apps/W1/Subscription%20Billing/App/Billing/Codeunits/BillingProposal.Codeunit.al#L237)) | page 8067 "Recurring Billing"; automated billing (`AutomatedBilling = true`) | 1, 2, 3 | the billing template (`Code <> ''`) | database record |
| `CreateBillingProposalForContract` ([L828](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/4c2cd7171f1e1c41bcb5f5893f67589d71719050/src/Apps/W1/Subscription%20Billing/App/Billing/Codeunits/BillingProposal.Codeunit.al#L828)) | page 8001 "Create Billing Document" (from a contract); pages 8033 and 8034 (usage-based billing documents) | 1, 2, 3 | temporary, from `CreateTempBillingTemplate` (`Code = ''`, `Partner` set) | database record |
| `CreateBillingProposalForPurchaseLine` ([L843](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/4c2cd7171f1e1c41bcb5f5893f67589d71719050/src/Apps/W1/Subscription%20Billing/App/Billing/Codeunits/BillingProposal.Codeunit.al#L843)), also through `CreateBillingProposalForPurchaseHeader` (L836) | page 8095 "Get Vendor Contract Lines" | 1, 2, 3 | temporary (`Code = ''`, `Partner` = Vendor) | temporary (`TempServiceCommitment`; the caller copies `Next Billing Date` back) |
| `UpdateBillingToDate` ([L768](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/4c2cd7171f1e1c41bcb5f5893f67589d71719050/src/Apps/W1/Subscription%20Billing/App/Billing/Codeunits/BillingProposal.Codeunit.al#L768-L789)) | page 8067, action "Change Billing To Date" | 3 only: it calls `CalculateBillingPeriod` and `UpdateBillingLine` directly, not `ProcessServiceCommitment` | the billing line's template | database record |

Subscribers can tell the contexts apart with values that are already in scope. No new parameter type is needed:

- **Template run or not:** `BillingTemplate.Code = ''` means a call from a contract or a purchase document. `ProcessServiceCommitment` uses the same test itself at [L354](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/4c2cd7171f1e1c41bcb5f5893f67589d71719050/src/Apps/W1/Subscription%20Billing/App/Billing/Codeunits/BillingProposal.Codeunit.al#L354). Event 1 already receives `BillingTemplate`. To give events 2 and 3 the same context, this update adds a `BillingTemplate` parameter to both (see the signatures above). It is in scope in both procedures: a parameter of `ProcessServiceCommitment` and of `UpdateBillingLine`.
- **Purchase document:** `SubscriptionLine.IsTemporary()` is true only on the "Get Vendor Contract Lines" path.
- **Change of "Billing to":** only event 3 is reached, with the line's own template. Our subscribers do not need to tell this apart from a proposal run, because the next period must start on the same date either way.
- **Usage-based lines:** event 2 fires after the existing `OnAfterCalculateBillingPeriodForUsageBasedSubscriptionLine`. A subscriber that handles only lines with a billing rhythm checks `SubscriptionLine."Usage Based Billing"`.

The existing `OnCheckSkipSubscriptionLineOnElse` is already raised in the same three `ProcessServiceCommitment` contexts, so event 1 does not reach any new context. It only adds the branches and the dates that are missing today.

### Provide an implementation (optional)

- [ ] I will provide the implementation for this extensibility request

title: [W1][Table][6010][Service Header Archive] Make SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter public and add its OnBefore event
description:
### Why do you need this change?

Table 6010 `"Service Header Archive"` implements [`internal procedure SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter()`](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/2f3b868dca78a5607e2b5054d3418156e5f803e4/src/Layers/W1/BaseApp/Service/Archive/ServiceHeaderArchive.Table.al#L1036). It is the only table in the W1 Base Application that carries this method but keeps it `internal` and publishes no `OnBeforeSetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter`.

A scan of `src/Layers/W1` at commit `2f3b868` finds **30 tables** that define `SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter`. Of those:

| | Count | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public `procedure` with the `OnBefore...` publisher | 29 | every sales, purchase, service and return document table, including both other archive tables |
| `internal procedure`, no publisher | **1** | 6010 `Service Header Archive` |

The current implementation, for reference:

```al
internal procedure SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter()
var
    UserSetupManagement: Codeunit "User Setup Management";
begin
    if UserSetupManagement.GetServiceFilter() <> '' then begin
        FilterGroup(2);
        SetRange("Responsibility Center", UserSetupManagement.GetServiceFilter());
        FilterGroup(0);
    end;
end;
```

Compare the direct sibling, table 5107 `"Sales Header Archive"`, which is [a public `procedure` with an `IsHandled` publisher](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/2f3b868dca78a5607e2b5054d3418156e5f803e4/src/Layers/W1/BaseApp/Sales/Archive/SalesHeaderArchive.Table.al#L1592).

#### What makes this different from a normal parity gap

Nothing in the W1 Base Application calls table 6010's method. Five pages are bound to the table and none of them has an `OnOpenPage` trigger or applies any responsibility-center filter:

* 6270 `Service Order Archives`
* 6267 `Service Quote Archives`
* 6271 `Service Order Archive`
* 6268 `Service Quote Archive`
* 6274 `Service List Archive`

The equivalent sales and purchase archive list pages do call it, for example [`Sales Order Archives`](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/2f3b868dca78a5607e2b5054d3418156e5f803e4/src/Layers/W1/BaseApp/Sales/Archive/SalesOrderArchives.Page.al#L254) and [`Purchase Order Archives`](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/blob/2f3b868dca78a5607e2b5054d3418156e5f803e4/src/Layers/W1/BaseApp/Purchases/Archive/PurchaseOrderArchives.Page.al#L292), both from `OnOpenPage`.

So an extension is currently the only plausible consumer of this method, and `internal` is precisely what prevents it from being one. An extension that wants responsibility-center security on archived service documents can neither call the standard implementation nor substitute its own through an event. Its only fallback is to re-implement the filter inside an `OnOpenPage` subscriber for each of the five pages by name, which covers nothing else that reads the table - reports, APIs, or any future Base Application caller.

#### Repro

1. In a new extension, add a codeunit:

```al
procedure Test()
var
    SalesHeaderArchive: Record "Sales Header Archive";
    ServiceHeaderArchive: Record "Service Header Archive";
begin
    SalesHeaderArchive.SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter();     // compiles
    ServiceHeaderArchive.SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter();   // does not compile
end;
```

2. Compile against application 27.0.
   *Expected:* both lines compile, since both tables carry `"Responsibility Center"` and both implement the method.
   *Actual:* only the sales archive line compiles. The service archive line fails because the member is `internal` to the Base Application and therefore not accessible from an extension.

3. Then try to override the filter on either table by subscribing to `OnBeforeSetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter`. The subscription resolves for `Sales Header Archive` and there is no such publisher to subscribe to for `Service Header Archive`.

### Describe the request

Two changes to table 6010 `"Service Header Archive"`, both confined to the existing `SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter` method.

1. Change `internal procedure SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter()` to `procedure SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter()`, matching the other 29 tables.
2. Add the `OnBeforeSetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter` publisher, identical in shape and placement to the one on `Sales Header Archive`.

Resulting method:

```al
procedure SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter()
var
    UserSetupManagement: Codeunit "User Setup Management";
    IsHandled: Boolean;
begin
    IsHandled := false;
    OnBeforeSetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter(Rec, IsHandled);
    if IsHandled then
        exit;

    if UserSetupManagement.GetServiceFilter() <> '' then begin
        FilterGroup(2);
        SetRange("Responsibility Center", UserSetupManagement.GetServiceFilter());
        FilterGroup(0);
    end;
end;
```

#### Event publisher

**EventRequest**

```
[W1][Table][6010][Service Header Archive]
[SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter]
___
Raised before the responsibility-center security filter is applied, so an extension can replace it, matching the publisher that already exists on Sales Header Archive and Purchase Header Archive.
___
[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnBeforeSetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter(var ServiceHeaderArchive: Record "Service Header Archive"; var IsHandled: Boolean)
begin
end;
```

#### Minimum requirements for the new IsHandled event

This request copies an existing `IsHandled` publisher, so per [minimum requirements for new IsHandled events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-use-ishandled-min-req):

* **Problem statement:** `Service Header Archive` filters `"Responsibility Center"` but exposes no way to reuse or replace that logic, unlike the 29 other tables that implement the same method.
* **Alternatives evaluated:** subscribing to the publisher on `Sales Header Archive` does not fire for service archives. An `OnOpenPage` subscriber on each of the five archive pages is page-scoped and invisible to reports and APIs. Making the method public without the event would let an extension call the standard filter but still not substitute a different one, which is the actual need.
* **Proposed publisher location:** table 6010, inside `SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter`, immediately before the filter is applied - identical placement to `Sales Header Archive`.
* **Proposed code:** the snippet above. Before: `internal`, no event. After: a copy of the sibling implementation.
* **Subscriber example:** `IsHandled := true;` followed by `FilterGroup(2); SetFilter("Responsibility Center", <filter>); FilterGroup(0);`.
* **Performance and data:** called once per page open or report data item, never in a record loop. Parameters are the record and a Boolean. No new fields and no new data exposure.
* **Multi-extension interaction:** the same contract as every existing `OnBeforeSetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter` - the first subscriber to set `IsHandled` wins, and subscribers are expected to exit when it is already true. Acceptable because a security filter should have a single owner.
* **Justification for `IsHandled` rather than a different pattern:** consistency. A skip-style event would arguably be higher quality in the abstract, but introducing a different shape on one of thirty tables would force partners to write two subscriber shapes for one rule.

#### Explicitly out of scope

This request does not ask you to change what the five archive pages do. Whether `Service Order Archives` and the others should call `SetSecurityFilterOnRespCenter` from `OnOpenPage`, the way the sales and purchase archive list pages do, is a separate question about product behaviour and would change what existing users see. It is mentioned above only to explain why the method currently has no caller, and why an extension is the only party that can use it. If that call is ever added, the publisher requested here is what makes it overridable.

#### Affected objects

Table 6010 `"Service Header Archive"` in W1 only. Unlike `Sales Line` or `Purchase Header`, this table has no localization-layer copies - `ServiceHeaderArchive.Table.al` exists in `src/Layers/W1` and nowhere else in the repository, so there are no counterparts to keep in sync.

#### Compatibility

Purely additive. Widening `internal` to `procedure` removes no member and changes no signature. The new publisher has no subscribers on an existing installation, so `IsHandled` stays `false` and the method behaves exactly as it does today. Since no Base Application code currently calls the method, there is no call site whose behaviour could change.

#### Relationship to #11448

[#11448](https://github.com/microsoft/BCApps/issues/11448) asks for multi-value responsibility-center filters, which would change how every implementation of this method resolves its filter. That request originally also contained this table-6010 parity item; it has been removed from it and filed here so that each request covers one change. The two are independent: if #11448 is accepted, the body of this method would use the text variant and `SetFilter` like all the others, but the `internal` to `procedure` widening and the missing publisher are needed either way.

### Provide an implementation (optional)

- [ ] I will provide the implementation for this extensibility request

title: [W1][Codeunit][427][IC Inbox Outbox Mgt.] Make GetNextICTransactionNo externally accessible
description:
### Why do you need this change?

Our extension adds additional Intercompany document types that are registered directly in the standard `"IC Outbox Transaction"` table. These transactions must use the same transaction-number sequence as standard Business Central Intercompany transactions.

Business Central previously generated transaction numbers through `"General Ledger Setup"."Last IC Transaction No."`. The current implementation in codeunit 427 now uses `NumberSequence` through the local `GetNextICTransactionNo()` procedure. The setup field is only used when initializing the sequence and is no longer updated for each transaction.

Because `GetNextICTransactionNo()` is local, extensions cannot safely obtain the next standard IC transaction number. Continuing to use `"Last IC Transaction No." + 1` would create a separate, unsynchronized numbering mechanism and could result in duplicate or conflicting transaction numbers.

Making this procedure accessible, or providing a public wrapper, would allow extensions to create additional IC transaction types safely while using the same concurrency-safe number sequence as standard Business Central.


### Describe the request

Please make the local `GetNextICTransactionNo()` procedure in codeunit 427 `"IC Inbox Outbox Mgt."` publicly accessible.

The procedure is currently defined as:

```al
local procedure GetNextICTransactionNo(): Integer
begin
    EnsureICTransactionNoSequenceExists();
    exit(NumberSequence.Next(ICTransactionNoSequenceTok));
end;
```

We request changing it to:

```al
procedure GetNextICTransactionNo(): Integer
begin
    EnsureICTransactionNoSequenceExists();
    exit(NumberSequence.Next(ICTransactionNoSequenceTok));
end;
```

Alternatively, a new public wrapper may be added:

```al
procedure GetNextICTransactionNumber(): Integer
begin
    exit(GetNextICTransactionNo());
end;
```

The public procedure should return the next transaction number from the standard `ICTransactionNo` number sequence while retaining the existing sequence initialization and concurrency-safe behavior.

comment 2: [[Author] (2026-11-06)]: ### Use of xRec

Our subscriber does not use `xWarehouseActivityLine`; `Rec` together with `CurrFieldNo` is sufficient to decide whether the line is ours. The parameter is included only so that the signature matches the existing `OnBeforeOverReceiptProcessing` on table 39 Purchase Line (`var PurchaseLine; xPurchaseLine; CurrFieldNo; var Result; var IsHandled`); table 7317 Warehouse Receipt Line also passes xRec. As `OverReceiptProcessing()` is only called from the **Qty. to Handle** OnValidate trigger, `xRec` there carries the table-trigger semantics (the line before the validated change), which would let other subscribers react only to an increase of **Qty. to Handle**. We do not rely on it. If you prefer a signature without `xRec`, that works for us as well.

### Over-receipt state consistency

When a subscriber sets `IsHandled := true` with `Result := false`, the only statement skipped is `Validate("Over-Receipt Quantity", ...)`. All over-receipt side effects live in that field's OnValidate trigger: default **Over-Receipt Code**, `Validate(Quantity, ...)`, `Modify()` and `OverReceiptMgt.UpdatePurchaseLineOverReceiptQuantityFromWarehouseActivityLine`. Skipping it therefore writes nothing: **Over-Receipt Quantity**, **Over-Receipt Code** and **Quantity** of the activity line keep their previous values, and the purchase line is not touched. Activity line and purchase line stay in the state they had before. No half-applied over-receipt can occur, and an over-receipt recorded earlier is not changed.

The rest of the **Qty. to Handle** trigger is not bypassed: with `Result = false`, the **Qty. Outstanding** check runs unless `OnBeforeValidateQtyToHandle` was handled. A subscriber that suppresses the over-receipt is therefore responsible for allowing the quantity itself through `OnBeforeValidateQtyToHandle`; otherwise the standard error "You cannot handle more than the outstanding %1 units." (Text002) is raised. In our case, catch weight items whose base quantity follows the actual weight within a tolerance, both subscribers apply to exactly the same lines (catch weight item, purchase order, **Qty. to Handle** > **Qty. Outstanding**). The surplus is then handled by our own quantity logic, not as an over-receipt.

description:
### Why do you need this change?

Our extension adds a field to `Prod. Order Line` that the user normally enters by hand. It is deliberately **not** derived from `Quantity`: when a user changes `Quantity`, the field stays as it is.

There is one exception: when *Replan Production Order* reduces a reserved lower-level line to its externally reserved quantity, the field must be rescaled in proportion to the new quantity. Otherwise the line carries a value that no longer matches its quantity.

Today there is no event between `Validate(Quantity, ...)` and `Modify(true)` in `DeleteUnreservedLowLevelProdOrderLines`. Generic table events (`OnAfterValidateEvent` on `Quantity`, `OnBeforeModifyEvent` on `Prod. Order Line`) fire for every quantity change (manual entry, refresh, status change) and cannot tell this rescaling apart from the rest. The only marker the report sets, `SetCalledFromComponent(true)`, is a global variable without a getter (`ProdOrderLine.Table.al:1128`, `:1599`) and is only evaluated in the delete path.

### Describe the request

Please add an integration event in `DeleteUnreservedLowLevelProdOrderLines` of report 99001026 *Replan Production Order*, inside the `repeat..until` loop, in the branch `ProdOrderLine.Quantity > 0`, directly before `ProdOrderLine.Modify(true)`. It passes the line by `var` and the base quantity of the line before `Validate(Quantity, ...)`, so a subscriber can rescale its own field by the ratio of the new to the old quantity. No `IsHandled` is needed.

EventRequest:

[W1][Report][99001026][Replan Production Order]
procedure DeleteUnreservedLowLevelProdOrderLines
___
Raise an event after the quantity of a reserved lower-level line was reduced and before the line is modified.
___

Requested change (lines marked `+` are added, lines marked `-` are replaced):

````diff
     local procedure DeleteUnreservedLowLevelProdOrderLines(ProdOrder: Record "Production Order")
     var
         ProdOrderLine: Record "Prod. Order Line";
         ExtReservedQtyBase: Decimal;
+        OldQuantityBase: Decimal;
     begin
         ProdOrderLine.SetCalledFromComponent(true);
         ProdOrderLine.LockTable();
         ProdOrderLine.SetRange(Status, ProdOrder.Status);
         ProdOrderLine.SetRange("Prod. Order No.", ProdOrder."No.");
         if ProdOrderLine.Find('-') then
             repeat
                 if ProdOrderLine."Planning Level Code" > 0 then begin
                     ProdOrderLine.CalcFields("Reserved Qty. (Base)");
                     if ProdOrderLine."Reserved Qty. (Base)" = 0 then
                         ProdOrderLine.Delete(true)
                     else begin
                         ExtReservedQtyBase := CalcQtyReservedFromExternalDemand(ProdOrderLine, Database::"Prod. Order Component");
+                        OldQuantityBase := ProdOrderLine."Quantity (Base)";
                         ProdOrderLine.Validate(
                           Quantity,
                           UOMMgt.CalcQtyFromBase(
                             ProdOrderLine."Item No.", ProdOrderLine."Variant Code", ProdOrderLine."Unit of Measure Code", ExtReservedQtyBase, ProdOrderLine."Qty. per Unit of Measure"));
-                        if ProdOrderLine.Quantity > 0 then
-                            ProdOrderLine.Modify(true)
-                        else
+                        if ProdOrderLine.Quantity > 0 then begin
+                            OnDeleteUnreservedLowLevelProdOrderLinesOnBeforeProdOrderLineModify(ProdOrderLine, ProdOrder, ExtReservedQtyBase, OldQuantityBase);
+                            ProdOrderLine.Modify(true);
+                        end else
                             ProdOrderLine.Delete(true);
                     end;
                 end;
             until ProdOrderLine.Next() = 0;
     end;
+
+    [IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
+    local procedure OnDeleteUnreservedLowLevelProdOrderLinesOnBeforeProdOrderLineModify(var ProdOrderLine: Record "Prod. Order Line"; ProdOrder: Record "Production Order"; ExtReservedQtyBase: Decimal; OldQuantityBase: Decimal)
+    begin
+    end;
````

### Confirmations

**Per-line event inside the loop, despite the per-iteration event invocation cost: confirmed.** The event is to be added inside the `repeat..until` loop of `DeleteUnreservedLowLevelProdOrderLines`, in the branch `ProdOrderLine.Quantity > 0`, directly before `ProdOrderLine.Modify(true)`. We are aware that it fires once for every retained lower-level `Prod. Order Line` in that branch, and not for deleted lines.

We accept the per-iteration invocation cost, because it is negligible compared to what the loop already does for each of these lines:

- `CalcFields("Reserved Qty. (Base)")` – a FlowField calculation
- `CalcQtyReservedFromExternalDemand` – a `FindSet` over the reservation entries plus one `Get` per entry
- `Validate(Quantity, ...)` – including all its triggers and table events
- `Modify(true)` – a database write including the `OnModify` trigger

The event call adds no database access of its own. Without a subscriber it is a no-op call. With our subscriber it is one in-memory calculation on the record passed by `var`. It also only fires for lines that are reserved against external demand and kept with a quantity > 0, which is a small subset of the order's lines.

**Subscribers remain limited to lightweight per-line in-memory adjustments: confirmed.** Our subscriber only adjusts its own field on the `ProdOrderLine` record passed by `var`, in memory, by the ratio `ProdOrderLine."Quantity (Base)" / OldQuantityBase`. It reads and writes no records; the report's own `Modify(true)` stores the change. No posting, no `Commit`, no UI.

**Old-value parameter: `OldQuantityBase` instead of `xProdOrderLine`: confirmed.** The full pre-validation record is not required; the base quantity before the validation is sufficient.

### Why a per-line event and not a before/after pair

A per-line event is the only placement that costs no extra database work. At that point the report already has the line in memory, holds the table lock (`ProdOrderLine.LockTable()`) and writes the line anyway, so the adjustment goes out in the same single write.

A before/after pair once per procedure would force a subscriber to read every lower-level line of the order before, keep the old quantities in a buffer, read the remaining lines again after, copy the report's branch logic to find the rescaled ones, and call `Modify(true)` a second time. That second call runs the `OnModify` trigger again (including `ProdOrderLineReserve.VerifyChange`) while the report holds the table lock.

### Provide an implementation (optional)

- [ ] I will provide the implementation for this extensibility request

title: [W1][Codeunit][6154][API Webhook Notification Send] OnBeforeShouldReschedule
description:
### Why do you need this change?

When Webhook notifications are sent to external systems and the system responds with HTTP 404, the notifications are deleted and included related subscriptions. For other error codes the notification is rescheduled.


### Describe the request

Many systems - including Business Central - will return 404 for a resource when the component is updated. E.g. when a updating an extension, the endpoint will be unavailable for a short period of time. 

This makes updating the client system verify fragile, as the lost notifications and deleted subscriptions often goes unnoticed until the client system tries to refresh the subscription.

By adding the integration event the Business Central implementation team can customize the behaviour to match the client system integration with Business Central.

In addition/or as an alternative, accepting 404 as a error code that should be rescheduled should be considered. The ressource was there when the subscription was made, so it must be semi-safe to assume the service still exists when sending notifications.

```    
local procedure ShouldReschedule(HttpStatusCodeNumber: Integer) Result: Boolean
var
    IsHandled: Boolean;
begin
    OnBeforeShouldReschedule(HttpStatusCodeNumber, Result, IsHandled)
    if IsHandled then
        exit(Result);

    if HttpStatusCodeNumber = 0 then
        exit(true);

    // 5xx range - Server error
    // 408 - Request Timeout, 429 - Too Many Requests
    if ((HttpStatusCodeNumber >= 500) and (HttpStatusCodeNumber <= 599)) or
       (HttpStatusCodeNumber = 408) or (HttpStatusCodeNumber = 429)
    then
        exit(true);

    exit(false);
end;
```

```
[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnBeforeShouldReschedule(HttpStatusCodeNumber: Integer; var Result: Boolean; var IsHandled: Boolean)
begin
end;
```

comment 3: [[Author] (2026-11-09)]: > Proposed code change: Please provide the exact code addition or modification with 5-10 lines of surrounding context in Codeunit 6154 API Webhook Notification Send, showing where OnBeforeShouldReschedule should be added.

The proposed code is already provided in the description : OnBeforeShouldReschedule 

> Alternatives evaluated: Please explain which existing events or extensibility patterns you considered and why they do not work for this scenario.

When sending a WebHook notification has failed, the HTTP status used to determine if the request should be rescheduled is hardcoded in Business Central. Often a web service will respond 404 for a short while - e.g. when updating the application (just as Business Central does when upgrading an extension). The ressource was available when the subscription was created, so it would be safe to assume that the notification url is correct.

> Justification for IsHandled: Please explain why an IsHandled event is required instead of a regular event or another extensibility approach without bypass semantics.

IsHandled is required, as we need to signal that the failed notification should be retried and the default logic should be bypassed.

> Performance considerations: Please describe the expected execution frequency of this logic and any impact considerations.

The event has no database operations and the subscriber would likely simply override when to reschedule the event. As alternative the event could enable subscribers to modify the list of HTTP statuses to reschedule, but it would required the subscribers to rebuild the list of events each time. Also, the event is only raised, when the notification fails, which under normal circumstances would not happen often.

> Data sensitivity review: Please confirm whether any sensitive data exposure is involved.

No sensitive data is exposed.

> Multi-extension interaction: Please acknowledge possible conflicts if multiple extensions subscribe and affect the handled behavior.

Multi-extension would be a problem if one extension would say that 404 should be rescheduled and another would say it should not be. To make this safer, the failed notification URL should be made available to the procedure ShouldReschedule and again to the event, so the extension can test on the failed URL and only reschedule of "known" notification URLs.

title: [W1][Codeunit][5826][Matched Order Line Mgmt.] Make codeunit public
description:
### Why do you need this change?

We need to reuse the standard matching logic from codeunit 5826 **"Matched Order Line Mgmt."** in our extension.

Our customer requires functionality similar to the standard **Get Receipt Lines** process. To provide a consistent user experience and avoid reimplementing Microsoft standard business logic in our extension, we would like to use the existing functionality provided by **"Matched Order Line Mgmt."**.

Currently, this is not possible because codeunit 5826 is declared with:

```al
Access = Internal;
```

As a result, extensions cannot access the codeunit and its exposed functionality.

### Describe the request

There was already a request for this in #29979:

**Codeunit 5826 "Matched Order Line Mgmt." - Procedures GetPurchaseOrderLines and ShowMatchedInvoiceLines from internal to public**

https://github.com/microsoft/ALAppExtensions/issues/29979

The request was closed and an internal work item (**[AB#632756](https://dynamicssmb2.visualstudio.com/1fcb79e7-ab07-432a-a3c6-6cf5a88ba4a5/_workitems/edit/632756)**) was created. However, in **Business Central 28.4**, codeunit 5826 **"Matched Order Line Mgmt."** is still declared as `Access = Internal`.

Could you please change:

```al
codeunit 5826 "Matched Order Line Mgmt."
{
    Access = Internal;
}
```

to:

```al
codeunit 5826 "Matched Order Line Mgmt."
{
    Access = Public;
}
```

This would allow extensions to reuse the standard matching functionality instead of having to reproduce the Business Central standard logic.

If possible, it would be great to have this change included in the next available release.

title: [ES][Codeunit][8060][Create Billing Documents] Add procedure and event to customize billing document grouping
description:
### Why do you need this change?

We need to customize the standard grouping logic for vendor subscription contracts when creating billing documents.

While sales subscription contracts provide an event that allows the standard grouping criteria to be customized, purchase subscription contracts compare the standard grouping fields directly, with no extensibility point available.

We need a similar event for purchase subscription contracts to customize the grouping behavior without modifying the standard application code.

### Describe the request

In codeunit 8060 "Create Billing Documents", sales and purchase billing documents currently use different patterns to determine whether a new document header is required.

For sales documents, this logic is encapsulated in the IsNewSalesHeaderNeeded procedure. After evaluating the standard grouping criteria, the OnAfterIsNewSalesHeaderNeeded integration event is raised, allowing extensions to modify the result and therefore customize the grouping behavior.

For purchase documents, however, the same decision is made directly within the CreatePurchaseDocumentsPerVendor procedure by comparing "Partner No." and "Currency Code":

```
if (TempBillingLine."Partner No." <> PreviousVendorNo) or
   (TempBillingLine."Currency Code" <> PreviousCurrencyCode)
then begin
    ...
end;
```

We would like the purchase logic to follow the same extensibility pattern as the sales logic.

We propose extracting this condition into a new IsNewPurchaseHeaderNeeded procedure and adding an OnAfterIsNewPurchaseHeaderNeeded integration event.

The procedure could be implemented as follows:

```
local procedure IsNewPurchaseHeaderNeeded(
PreviousVendorNo: Code[20];
PreviousCurrencyCode: Code[20];
PreviousContractNo: Code[20]
) CreateNewPurchaseHeader: Boolean
begin
CreateNewPurchaseHeader :=
(TempBillingLine."Partner No." <> PreviousVendorNo) or
(TempBillingLine."Currency Code" <> PreviousCurrencyCode);
 
OnAfterIsNewPurchaseHeaderNeeded(
CreateNewPurchaseHeader,
TempBillingLine,
PreviousVendorNo,
PreviousCurrencyCode,
PreviousContractNo);
end;
```

With the corresponding integration event:

```
[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnAfterIsNewPurchaseHeaderNeeded(
var CreateNewPurchaseHeader: Boolean;
TempBillingLine: Record "Billing Line" temporary;
PreviousVendorNo: Code[20];
PreviousCurrencyCode: Code[20];
PreviousContractNo: Code[20])
begin
end;
```

The existing condition in CreatePurchaseDocumentsPerVendor could then be replaced with:

```
if IsNewPurchaseHeaderNeeded(
PreviousVendorNo,
PreviousCurrencyCode,
PreviousContractNo)
then begin
...
end;
```

It is important that CreateNewPurchaseHeader is passed by reference to the integration event. This allows subscribers to modify the result of the standard grouping logic and implement additional grouping criteria without replacing or modifying the standard document creation process.

This would also make the purchase document creation logic consistent with the existing extensibility pattern used for sales documents.

This request is time-sensitive, as this extensibility point is required for an ongoing customer implementation. We would greatly appreciate it if this change could be considered for an upcoming minor update.

### Provide an implementation (optional)

- [ ] I will provide the implementation for this extensibility request

title: Event Request Codeunit 7312 "Create Pick" OnBeforeIsPickByExactRequestedUnitOfMeasure
description:
### Why do you need this change?

Codeunit 7312 "Create Pick", procedure `IsPickByExactRequestedUnitOfMeasure` (called in `CreateTempItemTrkgLines`).

Current code:

```al
local procedure CreateTempItemTrkgLines(ItemNo: Code[20]; VariantCode: Code[10]; UnitofMeasureCode: Code[10]; TotalQtyToPickBase: Decimal; HasExpiryDate: Boolean)
...
    if IsPickByExactRequestedUnitOfMeasure() then
        WhseItemTrackingFEFO.CreateEntrySummaryFEFO(CurrLocation, ItemNo, VariantCode, UnitofMeasureCode, HasExpiryDate)
    else
        WhseItemTrackingFEFO.CreateEntrySummaryFEFO(CurrLocation, ItemNo, VariantCode, HasExpiryDate);
...

local procedure IsPickByExactRequestedUnitOfMeasure(): Boolean
begin
    exit(CurrLocation."Directed Put-away and Pick" and (not CurrLocation."Allow Breakbulk"));
end;
```

Requested code:

```al
local procedure CreateTempItemTrkgLines(ItemNo: Code[20]; VariantCode: Code[10]; UnitofMeasureCode: Code[10]; TotalQtyToPickBase: Decimal; HasExpiryDate: Boolean)
...
    if IsPickByExactRequestedUnitOfMeasure(ItemNo, VariantCode, UnitofMeasureCode) then
        WhseItemTrackingFEFO.CreateEntrySummaryFEFO(CurrLocation, ItemNo, VariantCode, UnitofMeasureCode, HasExpiryDate)
    else
        WhseItemTrackingFEFO.CreateEntrySummaryFEFO(CurrLocation, ItemNo, VariantCode, HasExpiryDate);
...

local procedure IsPickByExactRequestedUnitOfMeasure(ItemNo: Code[20]; VariantCode: Code[10]; UnitofMeasureCode: Code[10]) Result: Boolean
var
    IsHandled: Boolean;
begin
    IsHandled := false;
    OnBeforeIsPickByExactRequestedUnitOfMeasure(CurrLocation, ItemNo, VariantCode, UnitofMeasureCode, Result, IsHandled);
    if IsHandled then
        exit(Result);

    exit(CurrLocation."Directed Put-away and Pick" and (not CurrLocation."Allow Breakbulk"));
end;

[IntegrationEvent(false, false)]
local procedure OnBeforeIsPickByExactRequestedUnitOfMeasure(Location: Record Location; ItemNo: Code[20]; VariantCode: Code[10]; UnitofMeasureCode: Code[10]; var Result: Boolean; var IsHandled: Boolean)
begin
end;
```

The procedure is local and has a single caller, so adding the parameters is not a breaking change.


### Describe the request

At locations with *Directed Put-away and Pick* and *Allow Breakbulk* = No, `IsPickByExactRequestedUnitOfMeasure()` makes
`CreateTempItemTrkgLines` build the FEFO entry summary with the unit of measure of the requested line
(`WhseItemTrackingFEFO.CreateEntrySummaryFEFO(CurrLocation, ItemNo, VariantCode, UnitofMeasureCode, HasExpiryDate)`).
`SummarizeInventoryFEFO` then filters the summarized stock by that unit of measure.

Our extension lets a pick take stock held in one unit of measure (for example KG) for a source line in another unit
(G or T) — one Take line in the bin content unit and one Place line in the source unit, without breakbulk lines —
independent of *Allow Breakbulk*. The bin search can already be extended through the existing event

title: [W1][Codeunit][6154][API Webhook Notification Send] OnBeforeShouldReschedule
description:
### Why do you need this change?

When Webhook notifications are sent to external systems and the system responds with HTTP 404, the notifications are deleted and included related subscriptions. For other error codes the notification is rescheduled.


### Describe the request

Many systems - including Business Central - will return 404 for a resource when the component is updated. E.g. when a updating an extension, the endpoint will be unavailable for a short period of time. 

This makes updating the client system verify fragile, as the lost notifications and deleted subscriptions often goes unnoticed until the client system tries to refresh the subscription.

By adding the integration event the Business Central implementation team can customize the behaviour to match the client system integration with Business Central.

In addition/or as an alternative, accepting 404 as a error code that should be rescheduled should be considered. The ressource was there when the subscription was made, so it must be semi-safe to assume the service still exists when sending notifications.
